claims.evidence: The introduction cites a reference supporting this finding from micromanipulation studies.

claims.claim: Manipulating the relative levels of euchromatin and heterochromatin altered nuclear architecture.
claims.source: In particular, manipulating the relative levels of euchromatin and heterochromatin altered nuclear architecture (Stephens et al., 2019a; Stephens et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites references supporting this finding.

claims.claim: Increased heterochromatin suppressed nuclear blebbing and maintained nuclear rigidity in cells with perturbed chromatin or lamins.
claims.source: Furthermore, in cells with perturbed chromatin or lamins, increased heterochromatin suppressed nuclear blebbing and maintained nuclear rigidity (Stephens et al., 2019a; Stephens et al., 2019b).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites references supporting this finding.

claims.claim: Loss of the lysine acetyltransferase MOF or its associated NSL-complex members KANSL2 or KANSL3 leads to altered mechanical properties of nuclei.
claims.source: Close interplay between lamins and chromatin is also illustrated by the observation that loss of the lysine acetyltransferase MOF or its associated NSL-complex members KANSL2 or KANSL3 leads to altered mechanical properties of nuclei (Karoutas et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites a reference supporting this finding.

claims.claim: Tumor cells commonly display nuclear morphology abnormalities compared to nuclei in surrounding tissue.
claims.source: For example, tumor cells commonly display nuclear morphology abnormalities compared to nuclei in surrounding tissue (Chow et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites a reference supporting this observation in cancer.

claims.claim: Mutations or alterations in expression of LINC complex components such as SYNE1 and SYNE2 result in misshapen nuclei.
claims.source: For instance, mutations or alterations in expression of components of the LINC complex (linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton), such as SYNE1 and SYNE2, which localize to the nuclear envelope and connect to the nuclear lamina, result in misshapen nuclei (Lüke et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites references supporting this finding.

claims.claim: Alterations to SYNE1 and SYNE2 have been observed in colorectal, lung, breast, glioblastoma, and ovarian cancer.
claims.source: Alterations to SYNE1 and SYNE2 have been observed in colorectal (Yu et al., 2015), lung (Ahn et al., 2014), breast (Zuo et al., 2011), glioblastoma (Masica and Karchin, 2011), and ovarian cancer (Doherty et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites multiple references supporting these observations in various cancers.

claims.claim: Misexpression or mislocalization of nuclear lamins has been documented in both cancerous cells and tissues.
claims.source: In addition, misexpression or mislocalization of nuclear lamins has been documented in both cancerous cells and tissues (Broers et al., 1993; Moss et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites references supporting this observation in cancer.

claims.claim: Lamin A/C is overexpressed in colorectal cancers, where it correlates with poor prognosis.
claims.source: Furthermore, lamin A/C is overexpressed in colorectal cancers, where it correlates with poor prognosis, and overexpressing GFP-lamin A in colorectal cancer cells increases cell motility (Willis et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites a reference supporting this finding in colorectal cancer.

claims.claim: Overexpressing GFP-lamin A in colorectal cancer cells increases cell motility.
claims.source: Furthermore, lamin A/C is overexpressed in colorectal cancers, where it correlates with poor prognosis, and overexpressing GFP-lamin A in colorectal cancer cells increases cell motility (Willis et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites a reference supporting this experimental finding.

claims.claim: Reduced lamin A/C expression is documented in carcinomas of the esophagus, as well as in breast, cervical, and ovarian cancers.
claims.source: In contrast, reduced lamin A/C expression is documented in carcinomas of the esophagus, as well as in breast, cervical, and ovarian cancers (Prokocimer et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The introduction cites a reference supporting this observation in various cancers.

claims.claim: The screen was performed in hTERT-immortalized dermal fibroblasts using two siRNA oligo libraries targeting 346 nuclear membrane proteins and 521 epigenetic and chromatin regulation proteins.
claims.source: We focused on nuclear proteins that may affect nuclear morphology via interactions that take place either at the nuclear membrane or within the nucleus. To this end, we screened karyotypically normal hTERT-immortalized dermal fibroblasts against two siRNA oligos libraries targeting 346 proteins that localize to the nuclear membrane and 521 proteins involved in epigenetic and chromatin regulation, respectively (see Materials and methods; Supplementary file 1A).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the experimental design and target libraries used.

claims.claim: Each gene targeted in the library was reverse transfected with three unique siRNAs in three separate wells.
claims.source: For each gene targeted in the library, immortalized fibroblasts were reverse transfected in 384-well format with three unique siRNAs in three separate wells.
claims.evidence: The results section describes the experimental methodology.

claims.claim: Cells were fixed and stained 72 hours after siRNA reverse transfection.
claims.source: Seventy-two hr after siRNA reverse transfection, cells were fixed, permeabilized, and immuno-stained with antibodies against lamin A/C and lamin B1, and with DAPI to visualize DNA and to assess changes to nuclear morphology (see Materials and methods) (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the experimental timeline and procedures.

claims.claim: Nuclear length, width, area, and circularity were measured simultaneously for all samples.
claims.source: To assess multiple aspects of nuclear morphology, nuclear length, width, area, and circularity were measured simultaneously for all samples, treated as independent parameters, and used for hit identification (Figure 1A, Supplementary file 1D).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the morphometric parameters measured.

claims.claim: The screen was performed in biological duplicates and results were strongly correlated.
claims.source: The screen was performed in biological duplicates and results were strongly correlated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The results section states this and refers to a figure showing the correlation data.

claims.claim: Genes were defined as hits if their median Z-score (two out of three siRNA oligos targeting the same gene) was ±1.5.
claims.source: Genes were defined as hits if their median Z-score (two out of three siRNA oligos targeting the same gene) was ±1.5 (see Materials and Methods for details).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the hit calling criteria.

claims.claim: Hits with a cell number Z-score of less than –2 were excluded to eliminate false-positive hits due to cell death, altered cell cycle behavior, or indirect proliferation effects.
claims.source: To eliminate false-positive hits due to cell death, altered cell cycle behavior, or indirect proliferation effects, we excluded any hits with a cell number Z-score of less than –2.
claims.evidence: The results section describes the filtering criteria to eliminate false positives.

claims.claim: Excluded hits included spindle assembly checkpoint components MAD2L1, BUB1, and cell cycle-related kinases AURKA and AURKB.
claims.source: As expected, excluded hits included spindle assembly checkpoint components MAD2L1, BUB1, and cell cycle-related kinases AURKA and AURKB, among others (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: The results section lists examples of excluded hits and refers to a figure.

claims.claim: 42 genes were identified as positive hits for nuclear shape in the primary screen, corresponding to a hit rate of 4.8%.
claims.source: Using this parameter, and excluding cytotoxic or cytostatic genes (see above), we identified 42 genes as positive hits in the primary screen, corresponding to a hit rate of 4.8% (42/867, Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: The results section states the number of hits and hit rate, with reference to figures.

claims.claim: Nuclear shape regulators identified in the primary screen included genes whose products localize to the nuclear membrane or nuclear lamina such as CHMP4B, LMNA, or the nuclear pore component NUP205.
claims.source: Nuclear shape regulators identified in the primary screen included genes whose products localize to the nuclear membrane or nuclear lamina such as CHMP4B, LMNA, or the nuclear pore component NUP205.
claims.evidence: The results section lists specific examples of nuclear shape hits.

claims.claim: 64% (27/42) of the effectors altering nuclear shape were genes whose products are involved in epigenetic modifications.
claims.source: Interestingly, 64% (27/42) of the effectors altering nuclear shape were genes whose products are involved in epigenetic modifications such as the polycomb component PCGF1, the histone acetyltransferase MYST3, the histone methyltransferase SETD2, or the ring finger protein RNF168 (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: The results section provides the percentage and specific examples of epigenetic modifiers.

claims.claim: LMNA was identified as the second strongest hit in the screen.
claims.source: As expected, and reassuringly, LMNA was identified in the siRNA oligo library as the second strongest hit in our screen (Supplementary file 2A).
claims.evidence: The results section states the ranking of LMNA as a hit.

claims.claim: Twelve siRNA targets reduced lamin A/C level by a Z-score of at least 1.5.
claims.source: Twelve siRNA targets reduced lamin A/C level by a Z-score of at least 1.5 (Supplementary file 2B) and 15 targets reduced lamin B levels by a Z-score of 1.5 or more (Supplementary file 2C).
claims.evidence: The results section provides the number of hits affecting lamin A/C levels.

claims.claim: 15 targets reduced lamin B levels by a Z-score of 1.5 or more.
claims.source: Twelve siRNA targets reduced lamin A/C level by a Z-score of at least 1.5 (Supplementary file 2B) and 15 targets reduced lamin B levels by a Z-score of 1.5 or more (Supplementary file 2C).
claims.evidence: The results section provides the number of hits affecting lamin B1 levels.

claims.claim: Of the 42 shape hits, only 4 affected lamin A/C and lamin B1 expression.
claims.source: Remarkably, of the 42 shape hits, only 4 affected lamin A/C and lamin B1 expression (Figure 1F–J).
claims.evidence: The results section states this finding with reference to figures.

claims.claim: The histone acetyltransferase MYST3 affects nuclear shape, lamin A/C, and lamin B1 levels.
claims.source: This groups included the histone acetyltransferase MYST3 that affects nuclear shape, lamin A/C, and lamin B1 levels, as well as the zinc-finger transcription factors EVI1 and LMNA which affect both nuclear shape and lamin A/C levels, and the proteasome component PSMA4 which affects nuclear shape and lamin B1 levels.
claims.evidence: The results section lists MYST3 as one of the hits affecting both shape and lamin levels.

claims.claim: The zinc-finger transcription factors EVI1 and LMNA affect both nuclear shape and lamin A/C levels.
claims.source: This groups included the histone acetyltransferase MYST3 that affects nuclear shape, lamin A/C, and lamin B1 levels, as well as the zinc-finger transcription factors EVI1 and LMNA which affect both nuclear shape and lamin A/C levels, and the proteasome component PSMA4 which affects nuclear shape and lamin B1 levels.
claims.evidence: The results section lists EVI1 and LMNA as hits affecting both shape and lamin A/C levels.

claims.claim: The proteasome component PSMA4 affects nuclear shape and lamin B1 levels.
claims.source: This groups included the histone acetyltransferase MYST3 that affects nuclear shape, lamin A/C, and lamin B1 levels, as well as the zinc-finger transcription factors EVI1 and LMNA which affect both nuclear shape and lamin A/C levels, and the proteasome component PSMA4 which affects nuclear shape and lamin B1 levels.
claims.evidence: The results section lists PSMA4 as a hit affecting both shape and lamin B1 levels.

claims.claim: For the majority of shape effectors (38/42), lamin A/C and lamin B1 levels were unaffected.
claims.source: However, for the majority of shape effectors (38/42), lamin A/C and lamin B1 levels were unaffected indicating that the majority of shape hits did not exert their effect on shape indirectly via altering lamin levels (Figure 1F–J).
claims.evidence: The results section states this finding with reference to figures.

claims.claim: siRNA knockdown of 50 of the 867 genes affected nuclear size using a median Z-score threshold of ±1.5, corresponding to a hit rate of 5.7%.
claims.source: siRNA knockdown of 50 of the 867 genes affected nuclear size using a median Z-score threshold of ±1.5, corresponding to a hit rate of 5.7% (Figure 2B and C).
claims.evidence: The results section states the number of nuclear size hits and hit rate.

claims.claim: Knockdown of 36 factors increased nuclear size whereas 14 resulted in smaller nuclei.
claims.source: Among the size effectors, knockdown of 36 of these factors increased nuclear size whereas 14 resulted in smaller nuclei (Figure 2B and C).
claims.evidence: The results section provides the breakdown of size increase vs. decrease hits.

claims.claim: 52% (26/50) of nuclear size effectors were chromatin or epigenetic modifiers.
claims.source: As observed for shape effectors, a large number of hits (52%; 26/50) were chromatin or epigenetic modifiers.
claims.evidence: The results section provides the percentage of epigenetic modifiers among size hits.

claims.claim: Factors which increased nuclear size included genes encoding nuclear pore proteins such as NUP205, NUP62, NUPL1, and NUP85.
claims.source: Factors which increased nuclear size included genes encoding nuclear pore proteins such as NUP205, NUP62, NUPL1, and NUP85 as well genes that encode components of histone modifiers such as SUPT7L and PRMT2.
claims.evidence: The results section lists specific examples of nuclear size increase hits.

claims.claim: Factors that decreased nuclear size included the PhD-finger protein PHF10, the deacetylase SIRT4, the acetylation reader BRD2, and the histone methyltransferase MLLT10.
claims.source: Factors that decreased nuclear size included the PhD-finger protein PHF10, the deacetylase SIRT4, the acetylation reader BRD2, and the histone methyltransferase MLLT10 (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: The results section lists specific examples of nuclear size decrease hits.

claims.claim: Of the 50 size determinants, none altered lamin levels.
claims.source: Much like for nuclear shape, nuclear size determinates did not exert their effect via lamins, because of the 50 size determinants, none altered lamin levels (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: The results section states this finding with reference to a figure.

claims.claim: Of the 42 shape effectors and 50 total size effectors, only one, the nuclear pore component NUP205, overlapped.
claims.source: Of the 42 shape effectors and 50 total size effectors, only one, the nuclear pore component NUP205, overlapped (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: The results section states this finding with reference to a figure.

claims.claim: 34 factors were identified as needed for proper nuclear shape in MCF10AT cells.
claims.source: In an identical screen using MCF10AT breast cancer cells (Figure 3), we identified 34 factors needed for proper nuclear shape in MCF10AT cells (Figure 3A and B; Supplementary file 3D).
claims.evidence: The results section states the number of shape hits in MCF10AT cells.

claims.claim: Only three shape determinants (LMNA, EYA1, and TRIM6) overlapped between fibroblasts and MCF10AT cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, only three, LMNA, and the transcription factors EYA1 and TRIM6, overlapped with the shape determinants identified in fibroblasts (Figure 3A and B).
claims.evidence: The results section states the overlap between cell types.

claims.claim: Among all shape effectors in both screens, nuclear shape scores showed limited correlation (r=0.301).
claims.source: More generally, among all shape effectors in both screens, nuclear shape scores showed limited correlation (r=0.301) (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: The results section provides the correlation coefficient between cell types.

claims.claim: KAT2B (PCAF) is expressed in both fibroblasts and MCF10AT, but after its knockdown only MCF10AT cells displayed misshapen nuclei.
claims.source: This observation was prominent for KAT2B (PCAF) which is expressed in both fibroblasts and MCF10AT, but after its knockdown only MCF10AT cells displayed misshapen nuclei (Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
claims.evidence: The results section describes this cell-type specific effect with reference to figures.

claims.claim: RNF168 is expressed in both cell lines but only fibroblasts displayed strong misshapen nuclear morphology upon knockdown.
claims.source: The same was true for RNF168, which is expressed in both cell lines but only fibroblasts displayed strong misshapen nuclear morphology upon knockdown (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: The results section describes this cell-type specific effect with reference to a figure.

claims.claim: GST-lamin A containing the entire Ig-fold and C-terminus (aa 389–646) binds directly to histone H3, but not to the other core histones.
claims.source: We find that GST-lamin A containing the entire Ig-fold and C-terminus (aa 389–646) binds directly to histone H3, but not to the other core histones (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the in vitro binding assay results with reference to a figure.

claims.claim: GST-lamin A lacking the C-terminal 80aa (aa 389–566) or the C-terminal region of GST-lamin C (aa 389–572) did not bind to histone H3.
claims.source: GST-lamin A lacking the C-terminal 80aa (aa 389–566) or the C-terminal region of GST-lamin C (aa 389–572) did not bind to histone H3, suggesting that the unique portion of lamin A present in the C-terminus tail is required for the histone H3 interaction (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the binding assay results with truncation mutants.

claims.claim: The lamin A tail (aa 565–646) was not sufficient for H3 binding.
claims.source: However, while the lamin A tail was required for H3 binding, this region (aa 565–646) was not sufficient for binding (Figure 4B), possibly due to its disordered nature (Qin et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the binding assay results and provides a citation for the interpretation.

claims.claim: GST-lamin A (aa 389–638) bound as well to histone H3 as the full-length lamin A tail (GST-lamin A, aa 389–646), while the aa 389–626 region did not.
claims.source: GST-lamin A (aa 389–638) bound as well to histone H3 as the full-length lamin A tail (GST-lamin A, aa 389–646), while the aa 389–626 region did not (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the binding assay results with truncation mutants.

claims.claim: Amino acids 627–638 are required for the lamin A-histone H3 interaction.
claims.source: These experiments identify aa 627–638 as required for the lamin A-histone H3 interaction.
claims.evidence: The results section concludes this based on the truncation mutant binding data.

claims.claim: The region aa 627–638 is deleted in the lamin A mutant isoform that causes HGPS.
claims.source: Interestingly, this is the region deleted in the lamin A mutant isoform that causes the premature aging disorder HGPS, which is characterized by extensive nuclear shape aberrations, including prominent nuclear lobulations and altered H3K9 and H3K27 methylation (Goldman et al., 2004; Shumaker et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The results section notes this connection to HGPS with citations.

claims.claim: GST-progerin (aa 506–664 D50) did not bind H3.
claims.source: In line with a possible role of lamin A-histone H3 interactions in HGPS, GST-progerin (aa 506–664 D50) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) did not bind H3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the binding assay results with progerin.

claims.claim: The addition of DTT increased lamin A-H3 interactions suggesting lamin A binds to histone H3 as a monomer.
claims.source: The addition of DTT increased lamin A-H3 interactions suggesting lamin A binds to histone H3 as a monomer and dimerization limits its binding (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the DTT experiment results and provides an interpretation.

claims.claim: Co-incubation of the C-termini of GST-lamin A (aa 389–646) and GST-lamin C (aa 389–572) reduced lamin A-histone H3 binding.
claims.source: Co-incubation of the C-termini of GST-lamin A (aa 389–646) and GST-lamin C (aa 389–572) in a histone pulldown assay reduced lamin A-histone H3 binding (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the co-incubation experiment results.

claims.claim: The addition of DTT reversed the inhibition of lamin A-H3 binding by lamin C, suggesting lamin C inhibits lamin A through dimerization at cysteine residues.
claims.source: The addition of DTT reversed inhibition, suggesting lamin C inhibits lamin A through dimerization at cysteine residues (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the DTT reversal experiment and provides an interpretation.

claims.claim: Mutation of C522A in lamin A alleviated the inhibitory effect of lamin C.
claims.source: The inhibitory effect was due to lamin A-lamin C interactions, rather than due to the presence of the GST moiety, since mutation of C522A in lamin A alleviated the inhibitory effect of lamin C (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the C522A mutant experiment results.

claims.claim: Lamin A bound preferentially to peptides which contained a methyl-methyl modification signature, including histone H3R8me2/K9me2, H3K26me2/K27me2, and histone H4R19me2/K20me1.
claims.source: Specifically, lamin A bound preferentially to peptides which contained a methyl-methyl modification signature, including histone H3R8me2/K9me2 (Figure 5B), H3K26me2/K27me2 (Figure 5C), and histone H4R19me2/K20me1 (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the peptide array binding results with reference to figures.

claims.claim: The GST-laminA signal was ~5-fold greater for histone H3R8me2/K9me2 than for histone H3K9me2.
claims.source: For example, the GST-laminA signal was ~5-fold greater for histone H3R8me2/K9me2 than for histone H3K9me2.
claims.evidence: The results section provides a quantitative comparison of binding signals.

claims.claim: Lamin A also bound to acetylated histone H3 and H4 peptides including histone H4K12ac/K16ac, H3K27ac, and H3K4ac peptides although at reduced levels.
claims.source: While most peptides with the strongest GST-lamin A signal contained dual methyl marks, we did find lamin A also bound to acetylated histone H3 and H4 peptides (Supplementary file 3E). These included histone H4K12ac/K16ac, H3K27ac, and H3K4ac peptides although at reduced levels (Supplementary file 3E).
claims.evidence: The results section describes additional binding to acetylated peptides.

claims.claim: Expression of H3.3 mutants K9M, K27M, or K36M decreased circularity of the nucleus and reduced nuclear size.
claims.source: Expression of H3.3 mutants K9M, K27M, or K36M decreased circularity of the nucleus and reduced nuclear size (Figure 6B–D).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the effects of H3.3 mutant expression with reference to figures.

claims.claim: Expression of histone H3.1 mutations had little effect on nuclear morphology.
claims.source: Expression of histone H3.1 mutations had little effect on nuclear morphology (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the lack of effect of H3.1 mutants with reference to a figure.

claims.claim: Expression of the mutants increased the variability in size and shape in the population compared to expression of WT-H3.3.
claims.source: Single cell analysis demonstrated that expression of the mutants increased the variability in size and shape in the population compared to expression of WT-H3.3, although no correlation between expression level of the mutant and morphological effects was observed (Figure 6B–D, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the single cell analysis results.

claims.claim: There was a slight increase in lamin A levels upon expression of either WT or mutant H3.3.
claims.source: In line with our observation of lack of correlation between lamin A levels and nuclear size and shape, while we find a slight increase in lamin A levels upon expression of either WT or mutant H3.3, the size and shape effects were specific to the mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: The results section describes the lamin A level changes with reference to a figure.

claims.claim: The size and shape effects of H3.3 mutants were specific to the mutants, not due to changes in lamin A levels.
claims.source: In line with our observation of lack of correlation between lamin A levels and nuclear size and shape, while we find a slight increase in lamin A levels upon expression of either WT or mutant H3.3, the size and shape effects were specific to the mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: The results section interprets the lamin A data in context of the morphology effects.

claims.claim: No effect of H3.3 mutants on lamin A localization was noted.
claims.source: No effect of H3.3 mutants on lamin A localization was noted.
claims.evidence: The results section states this observation.

claims.claim: Histone H3.3K27M mutations were identified in a subset of pediatric patients with glioblastoma.
claims.source: This finding is relevant since histone H3.3K27M mutations were identified in a subset of pediatric patients with glioblastoma (Khuong-Quang et al., 2012; Schwartzentruber et al., 2012) and H3.3K36M mutations were documented in chondrosarcomas (Behjati et al., 2013), which are also characterized by extensive nuclear aberrations.

claims.evidence: The discussion cites a reference supporting this clinical finding.

claims.evidence: The discussion states this characteristic of these cancers.

claims.source: Lamin A and lamin C consist of an N-terminal head domain followed by a long rod-like domain in the central region of the proteins and prior observations showed that the C-terminus of lamin A maintains an IgG-like fold domain and directly binds to DNA (Stierlé et al., 2003).

results.result: A high-throughput imaging-based RNAi screen was performed in hTERT-immortalized dermal fibroblasts targeting 867 nuclear proteins (346 nuclear membrane proteins and 521 epigenetic/chromatin regulators) using three unique siRNAs per gene. The screen measured nuclear morphology parameters (length, width, area, circularity) in biological duplicates with strong correlation between replicates (r=0.6992 for shape, r=0.8413 for size), analyzing typically >250 nuclei per sample with hits defined as median Z-score ±1.5.
results.evaluation: The screen design and execution are well-documented with appropriate technical replicates, adequate sample sizes (>250 nuclei per well), and strong inter-replicate correlations (C106-C110). The hit calling criteria (±1.5 Z-score threshold with 2/3 siRNAs) and exclusion of cytotoxic effects (C48-C49) demonstrate rigorous quality control. The methodology is sufficiently detailed for reproducibility.

results.result: The primary screen identified 42 genes (4.8% hit rate) as nuclear shape regulators in fibroblasts, with 64% (27/42) being epigenetic modifiers. LMNA was the second strongest hit, validating the screen approach. Distribution analysis showed population-wide shifts rather than subpopulation effects (p<0.0001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).
results.evaluation: The identification of 42 shape hits with LMNA as a positive control (C53) validates the screening approach. The enrichment of epigenetic modifiers (64%) is well-quantified (C52), and statistical validation using Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests (C112) supports the population-wide nature of effects. The hit rate and categorization are clearly documented.

results.result: Most nuclear shape regulators (38/42, 90%) altered nuclear morphology without affecting lamin A/C or lamin B1 protein levels. Only 4 hits (MYST3, EVI1, LMNA, PSMA4) affected both shape and lamin levels. Correlation analysis showed weak relationships between nuclear shape and lamin A/C (r=0.183) or lamin B1 (r=0.081) expression.
results.evaluation: The claim is strongly supported by quantitative data showing that 38/42 shape hits do not alter lamin levels (C60), with specific examples of the 4 exceptions documented (C57-C59). The weak correlations between shape and lamin expression (C104-C105) provide additional statistical support. This represents a key finding challenging the lamin-centric view of nuclear morphology.

results.result: The screen identified 50 genes (5.7% hit rate) affecting nuclear size: 36 increased and 14 decreased nuclear size. Like shape regulators, 52% (26/50) were chromatin/epigenetic modifiers, none altered lamin levels, and only NUP205 overlapped with shape hits. Nuclear shape and size showed minimal correlation (r=0.09597).
results.evaluation: The nuclear size screen is well-documented with clear hit rates (C61-C62) and specific examples (C64-C65). The lack of overlap with shape hits (only NUP205, C67) and minimal correlation between size and shape (r=0.09597, C116) are statistically supported. The finding that none of the 50 size determinants altered lamin levels (C66) parallels the shape results and strengthens the overall conclusion.

results.result: Screening MCF10AT breast cancer cells identified 34 nuclear shape regulators with minimal overlap with fibroblasts (only 3 genes: LMNA, EYA1, TRIM6). Cell-type specificity was demonstrated by KAT2B and RNF168, which affected shape in only one cell type despite being expressed in both. Overall correlation of shape scores between cell types was limited (r=0.301).
results.evaluation: The cell-type specificity is well-documented with quantitative overlap data (C69) and specific examples of differential effects (C71-C72). The limited correlation between cell types (r=0.301, C70) and moderate correlations for lamin expression (r=0.4097-0.4179, C118-C119) support cell-type-specific regulation. The biological replicates (C117) ensure reproducibility of these findings.

results.result: Lamin A directly binds histone H3 in vitro through its C-terminal region. GST-lamin A (aa 389-646) containing the Ig-fold and C-terminus binds H3 but not other core histones. Truncation analysis identified aa 627-638 as required for binding, while the tail alone (aa 565-646) was insufficient. The binding requires both the Ig-fold region and the C-terminal tail.
results.evaluation: The direct binding is demonstrated through multiple GST pulldown experiments performed at least three times (C127). The systematic truncation analysis (C73-C76) precisely maps the binding region to aa 627-638 (C77), with appropriate positive and negative controls. The requirement for both the Ig-fold and tail regions is clearly established through complementary truncation experiments.

results.result: Disease-causing lamin A mutations disrupt histone H3 binding. Progerin, which lacks aa 627-638 (the region required for H3 binding), does not bind H3. DTT treatment increased lamin A-H3 binding, suggesting monomeric lamin A binds H3. Lamin C inhibits lamin A-H3 binding through dimerization, which is reversed by DTT or C522A mutation in lamin A.
results.evaluation: The progerin binding defect (C79) directly validates the mapped binding region (C78). The DTT experiments (C80, C82) and C522A mutation (C83) provide mechanistic insight into the role of dimerization, with appropriate controls. The connection to HGPS is well-established through prior literature (C78) and experimentally validated here.

results.result: Lamin A binding to histone H3 is modulated by combinatorial histone modifications. Peptide array analysis (performed three times) showed preferential binding to dual methylation marks (H3R8me2/K9me2, H3K26me2/K27me2, H4R19me2/K20me1), with ~5-fold greater signal for H3R8me2/K9me2 versus H3K9me2 alone. Lamin A also bound acetylated peptides (H4K12ac/K16ac, H3K27ac, H3K4ac) at reduced levels.
results.evaluation: The peptide array experiments were performed three times (C128) and show clear preferential binding to dual methylation marks with quantitative comparisons (C85). The identification of specific modification patterns (C84) and secondary binding to acetylated peptides (C86) is well-documented. This provides mechanistic insight into how epigenetic modifications regulate lamin-chromatin interactions.

results.result: Oncogenic histone H3.3 mutants (K9M, K27M, K36M) cause nuclear morphology abnormalities, decreasing circularity and reducing nuclear size, while H3.1 mutants have little effect. The effects are specific to the mutants (not due to lamin A level changes) and increase population variability without correlation to expression level. Experiments used three biological replicates analyzing ≥500 cells/nuclei per sample.
results.evaluation: The H3.3 mutant effects are well-documented with adequate replication (C129) and sample sizes (C130-C131). The specificity to H3.3 versus H3.1 (C88) and independence from lamin A levels (C90-C91) are clearly demonstrated. The increased population variability (C89) and lack of dose-response (C89) suggest a threshold effect, which is appropriately noted. The connection to disease-relevant mutations strengthens biological significance.

results.result: Epigenetic modifiers and chromatin regulators constitute the major class of nuclear morphology regulators, representing 64% (27/42) of shape hits and 52% (26/50) of size hits in fibroblasts.
results.evaluation: The enrichment of epigenetic modifiers is clearly quantified for both shape (C52) and size (C63) screens with specific percentages and counts. This represents a major finding that challenges the traditional lamin-centric view of nuclear morphology regulation and is supported by the mechanistic studies of lamin-histone interactions.

results.result: H3.3K27M mutations are found in pediatric glioblastoma and H3.3K36M mutations in chondrosarcomas, cancers characterized by extensive nuclear aberrations.
results.evaluation: These are well-established clinical findings supported by appropriate citations (C93-C94). The connection to nuclear aberrations (C95) provides context for the experimental findings with H3.3 mutants, though the claim about nuclear aberrations in these cancers is stated as general knowledge rather than specifically documented.

results.result: Background context establishing that nuclear morphology changes are associated with disease and aging, nuclear morphology is plastic and changes during development, and prior work has implicated lamins, nuclear pore components, chromatin factors, and epigenetic modifiers in nuclear morphology regulation.
results.evaluation: These claims provide essential background context and are appropriately supported by citations to prior literature. They establish the rationale for the current study but represent prior knowledge rather than new findings from this work.
